description: Course editability gating. Enforce at the DATA layer (new migration 0019: RLS policies + a trigger/discriminator) and reflect in the edit UI: a DRAFT course is fully editable (creator may add/edit/delete modules, lessons, questions freely) and may be published (status -> 'published'); a PUBLISHED course may receive NEW modules (and new lessons/questions WITHIN those new modules) but all previously-existing content (modules/lessons/questions that existed at/before publication) is IMMUTABLE: no UPDATE and no DELETE of existing modules/lessons/questions, and no INSERT of lessons/questions under a module that predates publication. Admin override via is_admin() is preserved to match existing conventions. This feature is independent of FEAT-002.
steps: CHOSEN RULE (document this in your report, literal reading of the user instruction 'cursos publicados possam receber adições de novos módulos, mas conteúdos anteriores não podem ser alterados'): For a PUBLISHED course, allow INSERT of new modules and INSERT of lessons/questions whose owning module was created AFTER publication; forbid UPDATE and DELETE of ANY module/lesson/question of a published course that existed at/before publication; forbid INSERT of lessons/questions under a module that existed at/before publication; and forbid un-publishing or editing the course's own content rows is out of scope except: do not let modules/lessons/questions of a published course be mutated. A DRAFT course is fully mutable by its creator. is_admin() bypasses all of these.

Discriminator for 'new vs existing': the schema has no published_at today. Create migration supabase/migrations/0019_course_edit_gating.sql that (a) ADDS a nullable column `published_at timestamptz` to public.courses (idempotent: alter table ... add column if not exists), (b) backfills published_at = coalesce(updated_at, created_at) for existing rows WHERE status = 'published' and published_at is null, and (c) adds a BEFORE UPDATE/INSERT trigger function public.set_course_published_at() that sets new.published_at := now() when status transitions to 'published' (on insert-as-published or on update draft->published) and leaves it unchanged otherwise. Use create or replace function + drop trigger if exists for re-runnability. A module is 'new' (editable while the course is published) when modules.created_at > courses.published_at (or published_at is null, i.e. the course was never published). Lessons/questions inherit their owning module's new/existing status.

RLS: In 0019, drop and recreate the three write policies to split FOR ALL into granular INSERT vs UPDATE vs DELETE. Follow the drop-if-exists then create pattern used in 0011. Replace modules_write with: modules_insert (allow when course creator or admin AND (course.status = 'draft' OR course.status = 'published')) - note new modules are allowed even when published; modules_update and modules_delete (allow only when (course.status = 'draft' AND creator) OR is_admin()). This forbids UPDATE/DELETE of modules of a published course for the creator while still allowing admin override. Replace lessons_write with: lessons_insert (allow when creator/admin AND (course is draft) OR (course is published AND the owning module.created_at > course.published_at i.e. a NEW module)); lessons_update and lessons_delete (allow when (course is draft AND creator) OR is_admin()). Replace questions_write analogously via the lesson -> module -> course join: questions_insert allowed for draft course OR for a question whose lesson's module is NEW (module.created_at > course.published_at); questions_update/questions_delete allowed only for draft course creator OR admin. Keep the existing _select policies unchanged (do not drop/recreate them unless you re-create them identically). Preserve admin override (public.is_admin()) in every write policy. Ensure the policies reference the owning course via the existing join chains (modules.course_id; lessons -> modules -> courses; questions -> lessons -> modules -> courses).

Make the migration re-runnable and self-contained: it should drop the specific policies it manages (drop policy if exists modules_write/modules_insert/... ) then create them, create-or-replace the trigger function, and drop-if-exists/create the published_at trigger on public.courses. Add explanatory comments mirroring the style of 0011/0018. Do NOT modify existing migration files.

TS type-compat: adding courses.published_at changes the generated Database shape. Do NOT edit src/types/database.ts (it is generated). If any TS code needs to read/write published_at before the user regenerates types, use the documented boundary-cast pattern from src/features/crud/api.ts (cast at a single narrow boundary) or the NormalizeDatabase shim approach - do not break the build against the current generated types. Prefer NOT selecting published_at in client queries unless the UI needs it; the gating is enforced server-side by RLS, so the UI primarily needs course.status (already available) to decide affordances.

Guard the destructive save path: src/features/courses/api.ts saveCourseTree() currently does a delete-all-modules-then-reinsert on edit (draft.id present). That would be rejected by the new RLS for a published course (and would wrongly try to delete existing modules). Update saveCourseTree so that for an EXISTING course it does NOT blindly delete+reinsert all modules when the course is published: either (a) only run the destructive replace-children path when the (existing) course status is 'draft', or (b) for published courses only INSERT brand-new modules (modules in the draft without an id) and never delete/alter existing ones. Choose approach (a) as the minimum (gate the delete+reinsert on draft status) and additionally ensure that publishing a draft (draft->published) still works. Keep behavior identical for brand-new course creation (no draft.id). Document the approach in findings.

UI affordances: Reflect the rule where course content is edited. Inspect CreateCoursePage.tsx (route /create - currently create-only, always inserts a new draft and never passes draft.id) and the admin CRUD (src/features/crud) and CourseDetailModal.tsx. (1) In CreateCoursePage, when (and only when) it is editing an EXISTING published course (i.e. a draft.id is present AND status === 'published'), disable/hide the edit & delete affordances for existing modules/lessons/questions (the 'Remover modulo', 'Remover aula', 'Remover' question buttons and the text inputs for pre-existing content) and keep '+ Adicionar modulo' (and adding lessons/questions within a newly added module) available; keep a 'Publicar' action available for drafts. Because the page does not currently load an existing course for editing, implement the gating defensively driven off the course status/isPublished flag so it is correct if/when an edit entry point passes an existing course - do NOT invent a brand-new full edit route if none is wired, but DO make the component's edit controls respect an 'isPublished existing course' condition. (2) In the admin CRUD, the course 'status' remains admin-editable (admin override), which is fine. Keep changes minimal and consistent with existing component patterns. Document precisely which UI surfaces you changed and why in findings.

Tests: Add a vitest unit test for any pure helper you introduce for the UI gating decision (e.g. a function like isExistingContentLocked({ isExistingCourse, status }) or canEditModule(...)) proving: draft course -> editable; published existing course -> existing content locked, new modules addable. SQL itself cannot be executed in-sandbox, so cover the decision logic in TS. Keep tests co-located under a __tests__ dir following the repo convention.
acceptance_criteria: A new migration supabase/migrations/0019_course_edit_gating.sql exists, does not modify any existing migration, is re-runnable (drop-if-exists / create-or-replace / add column if not exists), adds courses.published_at + a trigger to set it on publish, and backfills existing published courses.

RLS write access is split into INSERT vs UPDATE vs DELETE for modules/lessons/questions such that: draft course content is fully writable by the creator; a published course allows INSERT of new modules (and lessons/questions under modules created after published_at) but forbids UPDATE/DELETE of existing content and INSERT under pre-existing modules; is_admin() still overrides. The _select policies remain functionally unchanged.

saveCourseTree no longer performs a destructive delete-all-modules-then-reinsert for a published existing course (the destructive replace-children path runs only for draft courses); creating a new course and publishing a draft still work.

The course edit UI disables/hides edit+delete affordances for existing modules/lessons/questions when editing an existing PUBLISHED course, while keeping 'add new module' available and keeping the publish action for drafts; the exact changed surfaces are documented in findings.
A TS unit test covers the editability-decision helper (draft editable; published existing content locked); `npm test` passes.
npm run typecheck, npm run lint (no NEW warnings beyond baseline), and npm run build all pass; src/types/database.ts was NOT hand-edited.
findings documents the exact 'new vs existing content' rule enforced, the published_at discriminator, and that the user must run `supabase gen types` after merge because courses gained a column.
verification: Structural review of 0019_course_edit_gating.sql (cannot execute: no live Supabase in sandbox) - confirm drop/create policy coverage, trigger, column add+backfill, and admin override.
npm run lint  (no new warnings beyond baseline)
